idiom_name: Express Router + route handler + res.render(view, locals)
implementation_notes: Express gives all four roles in miniature: an express.Router (or the app) dispatches by method and path, the route handler is the worker that awaits the service layer and builds a locals object, and res.render(view, locals) invokes the configured template engine (Pug, EJS, Handlebars) - app.set('views')/'view engine' perform the ViewResolver job, while engine helpers or middleware-injected res.locals act as view helpers. What replaces the classic structure is the middleware chain plus the view engine: there is no controller class, and a command-object dispatch table is justified only when the same endpoint must fan out to several actions or when a non-Express framework hosts the handlers.
pitfalls: Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async handlers: without try/catch (or Express 5) the request hangs instead of rendering an error view.
Module-scope state in the handler module is shared by every concurrent request; per-request data belongs in locals or on the request.
The locals object is an unchecked contract - a template reads properties nothing validates; centralising a view-model factory keeps it honest.
Template errors are reported through res.render's callback or the error handler, not the return value, so ignoring them hides a broken view behind a partial response.
